anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: After, like Before, re-dispatches plan-writer once as fresh/async false with the two FAIL lines verbatim under a Findings: block and explicitly states it does not edit the plan itself; after the byte-identical second FAIL it dispatches nothing further, makes no plan_tracker init, no phase_tracker complete, no SDD handoff, and surfaces the FAIL lines to the human as a gauntlet question; and at no point does it call resume or status or read the plan body. The only wording difference worth watching is After's closing sentence promising to re-dispatch plan-writer once the human answers — this is clearly conditional on a future turn and does not count as a dispatch, but if you want to leave no room for a judge to misread it, phrase it as 'the plan phase stays paused until the human answers' (as Before does) rather than describing the next dispatch concretely. Otherwise the After wording preserves every retry/halt fact while reflecting the renamed wave-file-disjointness check.
